title: Yisroel: the mind growing up inside the middos, from nursing to Keser Chabad
overview:
The chapter turns to *Zeir Anpin*, which is called Yisroel and Yaakov, and asks what the name Yisroel means: the *middos* run by the *sechel*, the Name *MaH* of *chachma* sorting out and ruling over *BaN*, *Elokim*. Its source is *Yisroel Saba*, the *middos* within *chachma*; the *middos* below it, born from the drop of *Abba*, are *Yisroel Zuta*.

Rabbi Markel teaches the rest as a child growing up. When a *midda* is born the reasons leave and only the outline stays: an angry man knows only that this is a bad guy. The newborn *middos* are an embryo, only stamped by the outside of the *sechel*. Through nursing, to six, they become ready for *mochin*; from six to nine the mind of *bina* gives conduct by reason, which a dog can never have; at nine *chachma* comes in and he thinks for himself. From thirteen to twenty comes *Keser Chabad*, the power to change the will itself, as the Rebbeim's limbs did the *halacha* by themselves. That master of his own nature is Yisroel, and most people, he says, never get past nine.

sections.title: Yisroel: the middos of chachma, Yisroel Saba and Yisroel Zuta
sections.summary: *Zeir Anpin* has two levels, Yisroel and Yaakov. Yisroel is the *middos* according to *sechel*: the Name *MaH* of *chachma* sorting out *BaN*. Its source is *Yisroel Saba*, the *middos* within *chachma*; the *middos* below *chachma*, drawn from the drop of *Abba*, are *Yisroel Zuta*.

phrases.he: (לד) והנה בבחינת זעיר אנפין דאצילות יש ב' מדריגות הנקרא ישראל ויעקב כידוע
וביאור פרטי המדריגות שבזה.
הנה תחלה יש להבין בטעם קריאת שם ישראל, כי שרית עם אלהי״ם כו'
והוא שם מ''ה שמברר ושולט על שם ב''ן כו', כי בחכמה אתברירו וכח הדכר לברר כו' האיש דרכו לכבוש כו'

blocks.text: *Zeir Anpin* (the small countenance) of *Atzilus* has two levels, Yisroel and Yaakov. Yisroel, "for you have striven with *Elokim*", is the Name *MaH* (forty-five) sorting out *BaN*, for "in *chachma* (wisdom) they are sorted out": the *middos* (emotional attributes) according to *sechel* (intellect).

phrases.he: וביאור הדברים, הנה תחלה יש להבין ההפרש בין ישראל סבא לישראל זוטא
שבחינת המדות שבחכמה עצמה נקרא ישראל סבא
ויש בזה ב' מדריגות, הא' מדות שבאור אבא, והב' מדות שבחכמה סתימאה
והוא הנקרא אדם קדמאה בלשון הזהר
וזה שכתוב מה שמו מה שם בנו כו'

blocks.text:
*Yisroel Saba* (lit. Israel the elder) is the *middos* within *chachma*: in the light of *Abba*, and inside, in *chachma stima'a* (hidden *chachma*), the *Zohar*'s *Adam Kadma'a*: not *Adam Kadmon*, but the upper *Yisroel Saba*.

"What is His name and what is His son's name", applied earlier to *Arich* and *Zeir Anpin*, is here the same in detail: the *middos* of *chachma* coming into *Zeir Anpin* when it is called Yisroel, not Yaakov.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the class's first, quick reading of lines 1-23 (201 w0-1273), before the tape is turned off and the chapter is read again from the start; the alignment marks the second reading.

blocks.text: On the second reading: "what is His name and what is His son's name" seems to speak of *Yisroel Saba* in *chachma stima'a* and in *chachma*, but it applies as well to *Yisroel Saba* and *Yisroel Zuta*.

phrases.he: ובחינת המדות שלמטה מן החכמה נקרא ישראל זוטא, כי הם בבחינת קטנות
לאחר שהן באין בבחינת הצמצום, והעלם עיקר עצם השכל
רק מה שהכלי חיצוניות דנצח והוד דאבא ממשיך להוליד ולהמציא שכל לחסד ואהבה, נקרא חסד זוטא כו'
(וכמשל טיפה במוח האב כו', כך נאמר מה שם בנו שהוא ישראל זוטא, שנמשך לו מטיפת אבא כו' וכידוע)

blocks.text: The *middos* below *chachma* are *Yisroel Zuta* (the small Israel), in *katnus* (smallness): only what the outer *netzach* and *hod* of *Abba* draw down gives birth to a *sechel* for love, as explained from chapter 25 on. The son comes from the drop of *Abba*, which holds *Yisroel Saba* both in *chachma* and in *chachma stima'a*.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the class's first, quick reading of lines 1-23 (201 w0-1273), before the tape is turned off and the chapter is read again from the start; the alignment marks the second reading.

sections.title: When the midda is born, the reasons of Ima leave and the overview of Abba stays
sections.summary: The reasons come to the *middos* through *Nehi* of *Ima*, and they leave at the moment the *midda* is aroused; the outline that comes from *Nehi* of *Abba* stays. Before the birth the love is hidden in the reasoning like a fetus in the womb.

phrases.he: והנה מבחינת נה''י דאבא נמשך בנה''י דאימא
שהוא בחינת השפעת והשפלת השגה וטעם למדת החסד כו'
אך בחינת נה''י דאימא מסתלקין בשעת תולדת גלוי התפעלות מדת האהבה וכהאי גוונא
כנראה בחוש
שמתקצר ומסתלק הטעם והשכל בשעת התפעלות המדה
phrases.en: The actual logical *taam* and the whole *hisbonenus* goes away at the time that the *midda* is *mispael*

blocks.text: From *Nehi* (*netzach*, *hod* and *yesod*) of *Abba* it comes into *Nehi* of *Ima*, which brings the reason down to the *middos*. When the love is aroused, the *Nehi* of *Ima* depart: **the actual logical *taam* and the whole *hisbonenus* goes away**; the *Nehi* of *Abba*, the outside of the overview, remain.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the class's first, quick reading of lines 1-23 (201 w0-1273), before the tape is turned off and the chapter is read again from the start; the alignment marks the second reading.

blocks.title: Why are you mad?
blocks.text: Ask a man why he is mad while he is mad. Later he could think through the *pratim* (details), but now they are gone, even their outside: to tell you what the other man did, he would have to stop and think, and stop being mad. The *klal* (the general idea) is there: what do you mean, why am I mad, this is a bad guy who did a bad thing to me. That is the very outside of the *klal*: *Nehi* of *Ima* gone, *Nehi* of *Abba* still there.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the class's first, quick reading of lines 1-23 (201 w0-1273), before the tape is turned off and the chapter is read again from the start; the alignment marks the second reading.

blocks.text: On the second reading he adds that this goes *davka* (precisely) through *tevuna*, *Ima tata'a* (the lower mother), as in chapter 2.

phrases.he: (והוא ענין וראיתן על האבנים כו',
שהירכים מצטננות
phrases.en: in women their thighs, their legs get cold

phrases.he: בשעת לידה
שנסתלקו נה''י הראשונים ונמשכים נה''י חדשים כו'
phrases.en: the first *Nehi* of *bina* are gone, and the second *Nehi*, *d'gufa d'Zeir Anpin*, comes through

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב במקום אחר)
ונקרא בחינת בקיעת יסוד דאימא
phrases.en: It goes through *yesod* of *Ima*, the connection of *bina* into the *middos*; you have to sort of break through it

phrases.he: להוליד המדה
ותחלה כלולה האהבה בהעלם מכוסה בשכל,
phrases.en: originally the love and the fear is actually included in the logic, but it's totally hidden

phrases.he: כעובר במעי אמו כו'

blocks.text: So in the body, **in women their thighs, their legs get cold** in childbirth, and they are given hot blankets: the first *Nehi*, of *bina*, are gone, and the second, of *Zeir Anpin*, come. It is called breaking through the *yesod* of *Ima*, the connection of *bina* into the *middos*.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the class's first, quick reading of lines 1-23 (201 w0-1273), before the tape is turned off and the chapter is read again from the start; the alignment marks the second reading.

blocks.text: At first the love or the fear is included in the logic, in the details and reasoning of the thing, **but it's totally hidden**, like a fetus in its mother's womb.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the class's first, quick reading of lines 1-23 (201 w0-1273), before the tape is turned off and the chapter is read again from the start; the alignment marks the second reading.

blocks.text: On the second reading: what goes over is just a *bechina* (an aspect), not the real outside of the *sechel* but an outside of an outside. In the intellect the *midda* is inherent.

sections.title: Three levels of mind in the middos, and the middos as an embryo
sections.summary: Once born, the *middos* grow through three levels of *mochin*: nursing, the first maturity of *Ima* and the second of *Abba*, at six, nine, thirteen and twenty. At the start they are three within three, like an embryo: only the outside of *Nehi* reaches them, a stamp of the *sechel*.

phrases.he: אבל לאחר שנולדו המדות
הרי הם כלולים מחסדים דאבא וגבורות דאימא בכללות ופרטות שלהם
phrases.en: And then they're made up from the *chassadim* of *Abba* and *gevuros* of *Ima*, in general and in particular

phrases.he: הרי יש ג' מדריגות: בחינת מוחין דיניקה ובחינת מוחין דגדלות ראשון דאימא וגדלות שני דאבא כו' כידוע.

blocks.text: Once born, the *middos* are **made up from the *chassadim* of *Abba* and *gevuros* of *Ima***, on three levels: *mochin d'yenika* (the mind of nursing), *gadlus rishon d'Ima* and *gadlus sheni d'Abba* (first and second maturity). Later the text gives a fourth: the inside of *Abba* and *Ima*, from the inner *Yisroel Saba*.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the class's first, quick reading of lines 1-23 (201 w0-1273), before the tape is turned off and the chapter is read again from the start; the alignment marks the second reading.

blocks.text: It is a whole big *inyan*. The basic levels are at six, nine, thirteen and twenty, each breaking down further, and not, poof, on the day: one to six is *mochin d'yenika*; six to nine starts the second; nine to thirteen the *mochin* of *Abba*, and at thirteen he is considered to have them, so he is *bar mitzva*, though only as far as *Chabad*. At twenty it is *Keser Chabad*: he can sell his father's property. Really going through it would take much more than ten minutes.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the class's first, quick reading of lines 1-23 (201 w0-1273), before the tape is turned off and the chapter is read again from the start; the alignment marks the second reading.

blocks.text: On the second reading he notes that the "etc." after the three levels means a fourth.

phrases.he: וביאור הדברים, בהיות ידוע שהמדות הם בבחינת עיבור
תלת גו תלת כו'
phrases.en: *Chabad* inside of *Chagas* and *Chagas* inside of *Nehi*

phrases.he: דהיינו רק חיצוניות נה''י, ובהם כלול בהעלם חב''ד וחג''ת כו'
phrases.en: the only *mochin* that's in the *middos* is in *Nehi*, and even that's a *chitzoniyus* of *Nehi*, but hidden inside of it is really the whole *sechel*

blocks.text: The *middos* are in *ibur* (gestation), three within three: ***Chabad* inside of *Chagas* and *Chagas* inside of *Nehi***, like a fetus with its head between its knees.

All that comes over to the *middos* is a *bechina*, yet the whole *sechel* is hidden in it. Their only *mochin* is in *Nehi*, and not just *Nehi*: *mamash* (literally) the *chitzoniyus* (outside) of *Nehi*.

phrases.he: והוא רק בחינת טבעיות המדות כו'

blocks.text: *Tivius hamiddos*, the nature of the *middos*: *teva* is like *matbe'a*, a stamp, and like *tov'u*, "they drowned", sinking in. It is what is stamped in. A listener offers "embedded"; he is not sure of the word, but likes "stamp".

blocks.title: The stamp on the back of a check
blocks.text: The *midda* is stamped from the very outside of the *sechel*, the conclusion: I like him or I don't. Later the book speaks of a seal stamped over and over from level to level. Books were first printed so, and people stamp the back of a check instead of signing: the letters stick out. Only the letters of *Nehi* stick out of the *sechel* and stamp the *midda*. A *midda* of *katnus* knows only: I'm happy, I'm sad, I like him, I hate him.

sections.title: Nursing to six: the natural midda, then conduct by reason
sections.summary: Through nursing the *middos* grow ready for *mochin*. A baby has only the stamped, natural *midda*, with a mind in great *tzimtzum*; at six there is enough *sechel* to explain things and expect conduct, unlike an animal that can only be trained.

phrases.he: וביניקה מתגדלים להיות בהכנה לקבל מוחין,
phrases.en: With *yenika* they grow to become just prepared to receive some *mochin*

phrases.he: והוא כמו התינוק שמתגדלים אבריו מיניקת חלב אמו כידוע
עד שבהיותו בן ו' שנה
phrases.en: Until he's six years old

phrases.he: יש במדותיו מוחין בצמצום

blocks.text: **With *yenika* they grow to become just prepared to receive some *mochin*** (a listener corrects the reading to *b'hachana*, "prepared"): he will think before he acts, and finally before the *midda* takes shape.

blocks.title: The baby and the toy
blocks.text: Like a baby whose limbs grow from his mother's milk. A baby's *midda* is instant and natural; natural or stamped, in Hebrew it is the same. Hungry, he shouts; say goochie-goochie and he laughs; another kid takes his toy and he gets mad. That is as far as the *sechel* goes.

Still, there is *sechel*: he understands that he wanted the toy and the kid took it; and *chachma*, higher than logic, holds the incident, for memory is from *chachma*. After a few times he hates that kid before he takes the toy: not an analysis of today's case but an overview, I know this guy.

blocks.title: The lollipop
blocks.text: But the mind is in a big *tzimtzum* (contraction), waking only the natural *midda*. Refuse him a lollipop and he gets mad; you cannot tell him it is bad for his teeth. **Until he's six years old**, when kids start school: there are *mochin* in his *middos*.

phrases.he: אך בבחינת הטעם ושכל לנהוג בכל דרכיו,
לא מדות טבעיות כבהמה לבד כו'
phrases.en: not just natural *middos* like a *behema*

blocks.title: The dog and the carpet
blocks.text: At six you can already explain to him that he shouldn't piss on the carpet. A dog you can't explain it to: he doesn't do it because you'll hit him. That is training; you never explained that the carpet will get ruined. You can teach a dog not to attack certain people because they are our friends, but that is not an explanation: his *middos* themselves are handled with love and fear. He sees you love this man, so he loves him; he knows you'll get mad, so he doesn't do it, without understanding why. A six-year-old can already be given certain reasons, but it is not a real *sechel*, only a *sechel* for the *middos* themselves.

sensitivity.reason: Uses a coarse word for a child or a dog relieving himself.
sensitivity.publishable: At six you can already explain to him that he shouldn't wet the carpet. A dog you can't explain it to: he doesn't do it because you'll hit him. That is training; you never explained that the carpet will get ruined. You can teach a dog not to attack certain people because they are our friends, but that is not an explanation: his *middos* themselves are handled with love and fear. He sees you love this man, so he loves him; he knows you'll get mad, so he doesn't do it, without understanding why. A six-year-old can already be given certain reasons, but it is not a real *sechel*, only a *sechel* for the *middos* themselves.

blocks.text: Reason only to conduct himself: a *hanhaga*, conduct, as a listener supplies the English. You can expect a certain conduct from him, **not just natural *middos* like a *behema*** (an animal).

sections.title: Nine: fit to give birth to thoughts of his own
sections.summary: From six to nine the mind of *bina* grows; at nine *chachma* comes in and he can think for himself what it is all about, and the *midda* itself can start to come from the *sechel*. The ages are a process, and most people never get far along it.

phrases.he: עד היותו בן ט'
phrases.en: at the time that he's nine years old

phrases.he: שאז ראוי להוליד
phrases.en: *ra'uy l'holid* new *machshavos* on his own

phrases.he: שאז הוא בחינת גדלות המוחין יותר,
דהיינו יותר מכפי המצטרך אל המדות לבד
phrases.en: it's already more than just an analysis of what the *middos* need

blocks.text: Until nine, when he is *ra'uy l'holid* (fit to give birth), with more *gadlus hamochin* (maturity of mind). Six to nine is the *gadlus rishon d'Ima*, by explanation: if everybody hits, they'll hit you back. That is pure *bina*. At nine *chachma* kicks in: **it's already more than just an analysis of what the *middos* need**; he thinks what it is all about.

The ages are general. Some can do it at six; *Avraham Avinu* began thinking about the world at three, with more *gadlus hamochin* than a normal person. And it is a process: no sixth birthday when, poof, he has *mochin* of *bina*.

And there are people seventy years old who never got to six. They're like a *behema*, with the natural *mochin* of an animal. Others' whole mind for conduct is how to get their way: they're nice to people not because they understand there is such a thing as niceness, but because they want to sell a product.

sensitivity.reason: Says some old people are like an animal, and that some are nice to others only to sell a product.
sensitivity.publishable: And there are people seventy years old who never got to six, with only natural *mochin*. Others' whole mind for conduct is how to get their way: they're nice to people not because they understand there is such a thing as niceness, but because it serves them.

blocks.text: So the ages are not exact: an older person may reach only six or nine, a younger one what the text calls twenty. And what it calls twenty you won't find in 99.9% of people; in most the most is nine, where one starts to think what it's all about. The text speaks of the ideal, a child growing up in a *frum* family studying Torah properly. In our world most people are somewhere between six and nine, maybe even between zero and six. Six means conduct by *sechel*, though only the *sechel* of "this is going to come back and haunt me", what goes around comes around: if I'm mean to people, if I get drunk and beat up my family. A great many people in our world aren't even six by this measure.

sensitivity.reason: Judges that almost nobody reaches the level of twenty, that most people stop at nine or below, and that a great many are not even at six.

blocks.question: If hardly anyone gets past nine, how come everybody becomes bar mitzva at thirteen?
blocks.text: Up to thirteen you won't find many. But they have the ability: the vessels of their brains grow up, without the emotional maturity.
At nine he is ***ra'uy l'holid* new *machshavos* on his own** (thoughts): not just what his parents told him is not nice, but what he himself sees is proper.

phrases.he: וגם יוכל להיות התחלת התהוות המדה רק מצד השכל והטעם,
וכשיחייב השכל להיפך יולד מדה הפכית,
עד שמדותיו רק על פי השכל
phrases.en: until his *middos* are only according to what the *sechel* is *mechayev*

phrases.he: מה שאין כן קודם לבן ט' אין בו מוחין,
רק לפי המדה
phrases.en: only according to the *midda* itself

phrases.he: שכבר מוטבע בו, שיוכל להתחכם בזה
שזה ימצא גם בחיות ובהמות, התחכמות במדתם למצוא טרף ומזון,
רק שבאדם נקרא חי שבמדבר כו'
phrases.en: it's called the animal within an actual person

phrases.he: ודי למבין.

blocks.text: And the *midda* itself can begin to come from the *sechel*. At six only the action follows reason: he is still mad, but knows hitting brings problems and robbing a bank gets you arrested. Here the *midda* can come from the *sechel*, when it obliges him to love, or the opposite.

The next side picks up the line: **until his *middos* are only according to what the *sechel* is *mechayev*** (obliges). Six ends *mochin d'yenika*; six to nine brings the *mochin* of *Ima*; at nine the *mochin* of *Abba* start, and the *middos* can follow logic.

Before nine his *mochin* are only **according to the *midda* itself**, clever within it. Animals have this too: a dog is cunning in finding food, and animals learn to act within human society. In a person, **it's called the animal within an actual person**.

sections.title: From nine, nine sefiros in each midda
sections.summary: From nine he is ready for the second maturity, of *Abba*, when the *sechel* rules the *middos*. Each *midda* is then made of nine *sefiros*, and once its *Chabad* has grown its *Nehi* can give birth; at six it had only *Chagas* and *Nehi*.

phrases.he: ומבן ט' ואילך מוכן לגדלות שני דאבא
phrases.en: There he's already ready for the second *gadlus d'Abba*

phrases.he: דהיינו שיהיה התגברות השכל על המדות
phrases.en: not just because the *sechel* is *mechayev* from logic, but actually the *sechel* is the main thing

phrases.he: (וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין כי מראש צורים כו' באריכות)

blocks.text: From nine **he's already ready for the second *gadlus d'Abba***. He goes over the ages again until they come out straight: zero to six is *mochin d'yenika*; six to nine the *gadlus rishon d'Ima*, logical control of his actions; at nine the full *mochin* of *Ima*, and from nine to thirteen the *mochin* of *Abba* grow.

The *sechel* overpowers the *middos*: **not just because the *sechel* is *mechayev* from logic, but actually the *sechel* is the main thing**, as explained elsewhere on "For from the top of the rocks".

phrases.he: ולכך ראוי להוליד,
phrases.en: That's why at that point he's *ra'uy l'holid*

phrases.he: להיות שאז כל מדה כלולה מט׳ ספירות חב''ד חג''ת נה''י
phrases.en: At that point each *midda* is already made of nine *sefiros*

phrases.he: שכאשר נגדלו המוחין דכל מדה בבחינת חב''ד, אז ממילא יש כח בבחינת נה''י להוליד ולד,
כי הא בהא תליא
phrases.en: the *holada* of *Nehi* comes after from the *Chabad*

phrases.he: (כמו שכתוב למעלה באות כ''ו באריכות)
ובהיותו בן ו' היה כל מדה כלולה מחג''ת נה''י לבד כו',
שהמוחין מצומצמין מאד, רק לפי צמצום הטבעיות של המדות כו'

blocks.text: **That's why at that point he's *ra'uy l'holid***: each *midda* has nine *sefiros*, and once its *mochin* have grown into *Chabad*, its *Nehi* can give birth: **the *holada* of *Nehi* comes after from the *Chabad***.

At six each *midda* was only *Chagas* and *Nehi*, the start of the *gadlus* of *Ima*: the analysis of what the *midda* should be, not of what it is all about, the *mochin* contracted to what the natural *middos* need.

sections.title: Thirteen to twenty: Keser Chabad changes the will itself
sections.summary: The second maturity of *Abba* comes in full from thirteen to twenty: he can "sell his father's property", own the *chachma* and change the will of the *midda* itself from above the *sechel*. So the Rebbeim learned *Shulchan Aruch* until their limbs did the *halacha*, and *Avraham Avinu* went even past that.

phrases.he: וגדלות שני, היינו מבן י''ג עד ך',
שראוי למכור בנכסי אביו כו'
phrases.en: he's able to sell the *inyan* of *chachma*

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת כחב''ד שבכל מדה כו',
והוא בחינת הטיית הרצון בכל מדה, מלמעלה מן השכל של המדה כו'
phrases.en: he can actually change the actual *ratzon*

blocks.text: Beyond what he is ready for at nine there is another *gadlus* in *Abba*: from thirteen to twenty he may sell his father's property: **he's able to sell the *inyan* of *chachma***, because he owns it, even the *sechel*. It is higher than *sechel*.

That is *Keser Chabad* in each *midda*, the will tilting it from above its *sechel*: **he can actually change the actual *ratzon***, not just follow the *sechel* while the *midda*'s will stays natural and the *sechel* only rules the heart.
Rabbi Markel has not met many people who can do this, so few that he can hardly come up with a good example of how it works.
He can move the *midda* itself from one domain to another: that is selling it, the inner will as it is in *chachma stima'a*, up to *gulgalta* (the skull), its very essence.

phrases.he: כמו על דרך משל שינויי צירופי האותיות של השכל, שבא מצד שרש ומקור של עומק השכל ממקורו העצמי דוקא
(כמו שכתוב שם במשל חכם מופלג כו')

blocks.text: It is like changing the combinations of the letters of the *sechel*, from the source of its depth, and this applies everywhere. As the outstanding sage can give you the whole thing in other letters than the explanation's, *Keser Chabad* goes above the *sechel*, and there he can change the will.
blocks.outOfPlace: He first reads lines 44-45 here (202 w802-849), in the middle of explaining line 41; the alignment marks only his rereading of them at w1294.

blocks.title: The Rebbe Rashab washes three times
blocks.text: The Frierdiker Rebbe said, as other Rebbeim did, that he learned *Shulchan Aruch* so well that his limbs did the *mitzva* by themselves; all the Rebbeim are so, back to *Avraham Avinu*. The Rebbe Rashab washed three times, holding the cup with a towel. Asked why, when it used to be twice: if I do it, it is in the *Shulchan Aruch*. The Mechaber in fact says three. Just watch a Rebbe tie his shoes: that is the *halacha*.
blocks.outOfPlace: He first reads lines 44-45 here (202 w802-849), in the middle of explaining line 41; the alignment marks only his rereading of them at w1294.

blocks.title: Avraham's hand and the knife
blocks.text: So "and Avraham sent forth his hand": his hand did not want to, knowing it was not really what G-d wanted, and he had to force it to take the knife because G-d told him to. That was the great test: past even the level where the body does the *halacha* by itself.
blocks.outOfPlace: He first reads lines 44-45 here (202 w802-849), in the middle of explaining line 41; the alignment marks only his rereading of them at w1294.

blocks.text: So the *middos*, down to *Malchus*, the deeds, come from above the *sechel*: the innermost will supplants the natural *middos*, so this is what he wants to do.

sections.title: Yisroel: a head and a brain, master over his own nature
sections.summary: Yisroel is *Keser Chabad*: the inside of the *middos* coming from the inside of the *sechel*. From the inner *chachma* he sorts out *BaN*, *Elokim*, and is master over his nature, the *tzaddik* who changes the will itself. This speaks of Rebbeim, not of a normal person.

phrases.he: והיינו בחינת ישראל,
phrases.en: that is what *bechinas Yisroel* is

phrases.he: לי ראש ומוחין,
phrases.en: I have a head and a brain

phrases.he: דהיינו בחינת כחב''ד כו'
שאז הוא בחינת גדלות המוחין ביותר, שיוכל לברר לבחינת ב''ן
phrases.en: then he can be *mevarer* the *bechinas BaN*

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת אלהי״ם כידוע,
משום דבחכמה, פנימית כח מ''ה דוקא שמבחינת הכתר דחכמה שבמדות כו', אתברירו כו'
phrases.en: the *birurim* don't come from *chitzoniyus hachachma*, it's from *pnimiyus hachachma*

blocks.text: And **that is what *bechinas Yisroel* is**: "*li rosh*", **I have a head and a brain**, *Keser Chabad*: the inside of the *middos* coming from the inside of the *sechel*.

That is the greatest *gadlus hamochin*: **then he can be *mevarer* the *bechinas BaN***, *Elokim*. There the *birurim* (sortings) really come from, and so he is master over *Elokim*, over his own nature: **the *birurim* don't come from *chitzoniyus hachachma*, it's from *pnimiyus hachachma***.

phrases.he: וכמשל חכם גדול ביותר, שיודע העומק של השכל ממקור הראשון, יודע יותר איך לברר וללבן להוציא הטעות כו'
phrases.en: He is *davka* the guy who knows the *omek hasechel* from the first source; *davka* he can be *mevarer* and *melaben* the *halacha*

phrases.he: וכן חכמתו עמדה לו להתפרנס באומנות או בריוח עבודה כו',
phrases.en: His *chachma* stands for him to do a *parnasa* in *umnus* or *revach avoda*

phrases.he: שנקרא תורתו אומנתו כו'
phrases.en: that his Torah is *mamash* his *umnus*

phrases.he: והיינו ענין האיש דרכו לכבוש כו',
שהוא בחינת שם מ''ה דחכמה שמברר לב''ן כו'
וזה שכתוב כי שרית עם אלהי״ם כו'
phrases.en: that you are master over *Elokim*

phrases.he: ודי למבין:

blocks.text: So a very great sage: **he is *davka* the guy who knows the *omek hasechel* from the first source** (the depth of the intellect), and he can clarify the *halacha*, and earn a living by it: **that his Torah is *mamash* his *umnus***.
This speaks of someone like Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai. *Keser Chabad* is Rebbeim, or very big people, not your normal person.

This is "the way of a man is to conquer", *MaH* sorting out *BaN*, and "for you have striven with *Elokim*": **that you are master over *Elokim***, the *tzaddik*, total master over his nature. As the *Tanya* explains, he does not only stop the *yetzer hara* (evil inclination), like a *beinoni*; he changes the initial will: "I hate them with utmost hatred".
The *Tanya* of today's study speaks of the *beinoni*: for him it must come *davka* through *hisbonenus* (contemplation) of the greatness of G-d. That is already obvious.

reviewQuestions.question: While a man is angry, what of his reasons is gone and what is still there? Which *Nehi* is each?
What does *tivius hamiddos* mean, and how does the stamp on the back of a check explain it?
What can you do with a six-year-old that you cannot do with a dog, and why is it still not a real *sechel*?
What changes at nine, when he is *ra'uy l'holid*?
What does it mean to "sell his father's property" at twenty, and how is changing the will itself different from ruling it by *sechel*?
Why is Yisroel "master over *Elokim*", and whom is the chapter really speaking of?
